```typescript
  selected_model: string,              // e.g., 'gpt-4', 'claude-3-opus'
  precedence_tier: number,             // 1–6, using the versioned MS-005/099 source order
```

**MS-135 resolver record example (2026-11-25).** The resolver record is the shared record from "Resolver inputs and emit shape" above; that section stays the authority for its fields. The MS-135 spellings below carry exactly the same values under the names that fallback, clamp and picker consumers read. A record where an MS-135 spelling and its emit-shape field differ is invalid and is rejected with `resolver_record_invalid`.

| MS-135 field | Same value as | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requested_model_id` | `requested_model` | string |
| `requested_provider_id?` | `requested_platform` | string, omitted when no provider was requested |
| `account_id?` | `effective_account_id?` | string, omitted when the route has no account |
| `resolved_model_id` | `effective_model` | string |

Fields only MS-135 adds:

| Field | Type | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capability_snapshot_ref` | string | Ref of the §10.4.3 capability snapshot the resolver read. |
| `credential_route_epoch_id` | string | The MA-067 credential route epoch the effective account used. |
| `fallback_used` | boolean | `true` only when `resolved_model_id` came from a `fallback_chain[]` entry instead of the precedence winner. |
| `clamp_reason?` | string, closed to these members of the `clamp/substitution` reason-code family ("Provider capability and cost gating" above): `effort_unsupported`, `effort_clamped`, `auth_family_capability_clamped`, `capability_unknown`, `instruction_projection_partial`, `skill_projection_partial` | Present only when a requested value was not applied exactly for a reason other than model fallback, with the family's meanings (`effort_clamped` = accepted but narrowed effort; `effort_unsupported` = the effort control is unsupported). The model-level family codes `model_unavailable`, `model_routed_by_provider` and `model_substituted` are never written here: model fallback is `fallback_used = true` with `selection_reason.fallback_reason`. When more than one code applies, the first in this list is recorded and the others stay in the attempt's `EffortSettlementReceipt` and `skipped_persona_controls[]`. Why an effort was narrowed (model maximum, policy ceiling, budget, provider mapping) is the attempt's `EffortSettlementReceipt.clamp_reason`, not this field. |
| `visibility_state` | string, closed: `visible`, `visible_with_notice`, `hidden_from_picker`, `history_only` | Derived from the effective model's `model_lifecycle_state` by the model lifecycle table below. |

**MS-135 model lifecycle transitions (2026-11-25).** `model_lifecycle_state` (§4.1, CV-144) is a catalog-entry state, separate from the provider lifecycle in the acceptance criteria above. A model is dispatchable only when its own state allows it and its provider's state is `healthy` or `degraded`. The allowed transitions are exactly these; every other transition is invalid. A failed or partial catalog refresh never changes `model_lifecycle_state`. Each transition records `from_state`, `to_state`, `trigger`, `evidence_ref` and `transitioned_at_utc`.

| From | To | Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `deprecated` | A successful catalog refresh or provider metadata marks the model deprecated; `deprecation_notice_ref?` is recorded. |
| `active` | `sunset_pending` | The provider announces an end date; `sunset_at_utc` and `replacement_model_id?` are recorded. |
| `deprecated` | `sunset_pending` | The provider announces an end date for a deprecated model. |
| `deprecated` | `active` | A later successful catalog refresh no longer marks the model deprecated. |
| `sunset_pending` | `deprecated` | The provider withdraws the end date but keeps the deprecation. |
| `sunset_pending` | `sunset` | `sunset_at_utc` passes. |
| `active`, `deprecated` or `sunset_pending` | `sunset` | The provider stops serving the model before any announced date: a dispatch returns the provider's model-not-found error and the next successful catalog refresh omits the model. |
| `sunset` | `removed` | The provider explicitly lists the model as removed, or two consecutive successful catalog refreshes at least 24 hours apart omit it. |

`removed` is terminal for that catalog entry. If a provider later lists the same model id again, PM creates a new catalog entry generation that starts in `active`; history keeps the removed generation and its receipts.

### 3.4 `model_override` extraction

Keyword form:
```
(?is)\b(?:using|with|via|use|model)\s*(?:[:=]\s*)?(?P<model>@?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/\-\s]{0,80}?)(?=(?:\s*(?:,|;|\)|\]|\.$|$))|\s+\b(?:for|aspect|ratio|size|resolution|format|voice|duration|negative|quality|seed|bpm|variations?|versions?|options?)\b)
```
```
(?i)(?<!\w)@(?P<model2>[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/\-]{1,64})(?!\w)
```

The two patterns above use lookahead and lookbehind, which Rust `regex` does not support (see "Regex Engine Constraint For Prompt Slot Extraction"). They are kept as source lineage and as the behaviour reference only; implementations MUST use these two canonical lookaround-free matchers instead (2026-11-25). They produce the same `model` and `model2` values at the same positions.

Canonical keyword form (the `model_end` group consumes the boundary text the old lookahead only tested; the extracted value is `model` alone, and prompt cleaning removes the text from the match start to the end of `model`, never the `model_end` text):
```
(?is)\b(?:using|with|via|use|model)\s*(?:[:=]\s*)?(?P<model>@?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/\-\s]{0,80}?)(?P<model_end>\s*(?:,|;|\)|\]|\.$|$)|\s+\b(?:for|aspect|ratio|size|resolution|format|voice|duration|negative|quality|seed|bpm|variations?|versions?|options?)\b)
```
Canonical `@` shorthand (`\B` before `@` means no word character precedes it; the final character class with `\b` or `\B` means no word character follows the token, without consuming it):
```
(?i)\B@(?P<model2>[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/\-]{0,63}(?:[a-z0-9_]\b|[./\-]\B))
```

**Normalize model key:** lowercase; collapse spaces, underscores, and hyphens.

**Resolution order:** alias → exact model id → exact displayName → else `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`.

**Canonical media model aliases** (e.g., "Nano Banana", "Nano Banana Pro", "Veo fast", "TTS flash", "TTS pro") are defined in `Plans/Models_System.md` [§6.8](Plans/Models_System.md#MEDIA-ALIASES) (SSOT). Do not restate the alias table here. People add or override nicknames in the one Model nicknames list for chat and media models, `ai.models.model-alias` (Models_System §6.7); Media has no nickname setting of its own (DL-479).

### Regex Engine Constraint For Prompt Slot Extraction

Repairs row `sfk-471e24039fccbc4a5c93be12`.

- Prompt-slot extraction uses Rust `regex` syntax only.
- Lookaround patterns such as `(?<!...)` or `(?=...)` are forbidden in canonical patterns.
- Word-boundary behavior must be expressed with explicit capture groups and boundary tokens, e.g. `(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\{slot_name\\}([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)`, with the slot captured separately from the boundary characters.
- Any future use of a different regex engine must name the crate and feature flag in this document before patterns may rely on lookaround.
- The only lookaround patterns left in this document are the two `model_override` matchers kept as source lineage in §3.4, Appendix A and MGAC-043; §3.4 gives their canonical lookaround-free replacements, and no other slot pattern uses lookaround (2026-11-25).

## Appendix A. Slot extraction rules (regex-ish, deterministic)

1) Pre-processing:
- Keep raw (original) and s_lower (normalized lowercased).
- If trailing controls block exists (ends with (...) or [...] and contains control tokens), split body + controls and parse controls first; remove block from prompt.
Controls-block regex: (?is)^(?P<body>.*?)(?:\s*(?P<bracket>\(|\[)\s*(?P<controls>[^)\]]{1,400})\s*(?:\)|\])\s*)$
Control token gate: \b(model|aspect|ratio|size|resolution|duration|voice|format|bpm|seed|negative|quality)\b
2) kind detection:
- Prefix form: (?is)^\s*(?P<prefix>image|video|tts|music)\s*:\s*
- Else keyword-based:
image: \b(image|picture|photo|logo|poster|thumbnail|cover)\b
video: \b(video|clip|animation|broll|b-roll)\b
tts: \b(tts|text to speech|read aloud|say this|voiceover|voice-over)\b
music: \b(music|song|beat|instrumental|soundtrack)\b
- Else verb fallback only if unambiguous.
3) Precedence: controls block key/values override everything then: model_override, count, aspect_ratio, size/resolution, duration, format, voice/style, quality, seed, bpm, negative_prompt
4) model_override:
Keyword form: (?is)\b(?:using|with|via|use|model)\s*(?:[:=]\s*)?(?P<model>@?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/\-\s]{0,80}?)(?=(?:\s*(?:,|;|\)|\]|\.$|$))|\s+\b(?:for|aspect|ratio|size|resolution|format|voice|duration|negative|quality|seed|bpm|variations?|versions?|options?)\b)
@ shorthand: (?i)(?<!\w)@(?P<model2>[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/\-]{1,64})(?!\w)
(The two model_override patterns above are source lineage; the canonical lookaround-free matchers are in §3.4.)
Normalize model key: lowercase; collapse spaces/underscores/hyphens.
Resolve: alias -> exact model id -> exact displayName -> else MODEL_UNAVAILABLE.
5) count:
digits: (?i)\b(?:(?:make|generate|create|give me|output|render)\s+)?(?P<count>\d{1,2})\s*(?:x\s*)?(?:variations?|versions?|options?|images?|pics?|pictures?|clips?|frames?)\b
optional words one-ten similar.
Clamp to safe max (default 8). Last match wins.
6) aspect_ratio:
numeric: (?i)\b(?P<ar_w>\d{1,2})\s*:\s*(?P<ar_h>\d{1,2})\b
named: (?i)\b(?P<ar_named>square|portrait|landscape|vertical|horizontal|widescreen)\b
Mapping: square=1:1; portrait/vertical=9:16; landscape/horizontal/widescreen=16:9.
7) size/resolution:
Image keyworded: (?i)\b(?:size|resolution|res)\s*[:=]?\s*(?P<size_px>512|768|1024|1152|1280|1536|2048|3072|4096)\s*(?:px|pixels)?\b
Image keyworded k: (?i)\b(?:size|resolution|res)\s*[:=]?\s*(?P<size_k>2k|4k|8k)\b
Video: (?i)\b(?P<vres>720p|1080p|1440p|2160p|4k)\b
Do not treat bare numbers as size unless they are in controls block or trailing comma controls.
Envelope mapping: size_px -> size; size_k -> size (2k=2048,4k=4096,8k=8192) plus resolution token; vres -> resolution for video and MUST NOT override size_k-derived resolution for image prompts.
ContractRef: ToolID:media.generate, PolicyRule:Decision_Policy.md§2
8) duration (video/music only):
keyworded: (?i)\b(?:for|duration|length)\s*(?P<secs>\d{1,3}(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?:s|sec|secs|second|seconds)\b
bare (only in controls block or trailing controls): (?i)\b(?P<secs2>\d{1,3}(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?:s|sec|secs)\b
9) format: (?i)\b(?:format|output|export|as)\s*[:=]?\s*(?P<fmt>png|jpg|jpeg|webp|gif|mp4|mov|wav|mp3|flac|pcm16)\b
10) voice (tts):
voice id: (?i)\bvoice\s*[:=]\s*(?P<voice>[a-z0-9][a-z0-9 _\-]{0,32})\b
voice style: (?i)\bin\s+a[n]?\s+(?P<voice_style>[^,.;]{1,40})\s+voice\b
11) quality: (?i)\b(?P<qual>draft|standard|high)\b optional phrase mapping. Guard: set only when in controls block or quality-keyword phrase; bare descriptive adjectives in creative prompt MUST NOT set quality.
ContractRef: ToolID:media.generate, PolicyRule:Decision_Policy.md§2
12) seed: (?i)\bseed\s*[:=]?\s*(?P<seed>\d{1,10})\b
13) bpm: (?i)\b(?P<bpm>\d{2,3})\s*bpm\b|\bbpm\s*[:=]\s*(?P<bpm2>\d{2,3})\b
14) negative_prompt:
explicit: (?is)\bnegative\s+prompt\s*[:=]\s*(?P<neg>"[^"]{1,200}"|'[^']{1,200}'|[^,;\n]{1,200})
avoid-clauses (collect all): (?is)\b(?:without|no|avoid)\s+(?P<avoid>[^,.;\n]{1,80})
Combine explicit + avoid list (dedupe preserve order).
15) prompt cleaning:
- If controls block present: remove it.
- Remove only matched spans introduced by control keywords (using/model/size/aspect/etc).
- Preserve remaining text as the creative prompt.

### Reuse on Dashboard via Add-Widget Flow

All widgets that appear on the Usage page are **also hostable on the Dashboard**. Users can add any Usage widget to the Dashboard through the add-widget flow (`Plans/Widget_System.md#WS-030`, Catalogue; Widget_System's section 4 is the Orchestrator Progress catalog, so the former "section 4" citation and the `#4` ContractRef below resolve to WS-030):

1. On the Dashboard, click "Add Widget".
2. The catalog overlay shows all Dashboard-compatible widgets, including all Usage widgets.
3. Select a widget (e.g., `widget.quota_summary`) and click "Add".
4. The widget appears on the Dashboard grid with its default size.
5. Configure and resize as needed.

This means users can build a Dashboard that includes usage information alongside orchestrator status and other widgets, without needing to navigate to the Usage page.

## 2. Hostability and data contracts
Amended 2026-10-09 (DL-180): the Dashboard is now a tab kind in the home centre, and several dashboard tabs may be open, each showing one board with its own widget layout under `widget_layout:v1:dashboard:<board_id>`; any Usage widget can be placed on a board (`Plans/usage-feature.md#UF-062`). WS-030 owns the boards, their namespaces and the catalogue. The two rules below that named one Dashboard namespace and "some" Usage widgets are amended in place.

Amended 2026-10-10 (DL-186): every dashboard tab's board is a board of the Usage board engine, the engine the Usage page runs, and each board's contents are kept per project under `widget_layout:v1:<project_id>:<board_id>`; the 2026-10-09 form `widget_layout:v1:dashboard:<board_id>` was never written. Boards and their catalogue are built for several widget sources: Usage today, the Orchestrator after its own redesign, others later. Until then the old Home widgets and the curated `Progress` subset are on no dashboard. WS-030 owns all of this.

Amended 2026-11-12 (DL-477): a Goals source and a Workflows source join Usage in the board engine's registry of widget sources, and the Home board's default set holds their four widgets with Usage's `widget.alert_thresholds`: Active goals, Stuck or blocked goals, Verification and repair status, Certification state, and Cost and budget warnings, each removable like any other widget. The per-project clauses below describe the Project board variant. WS-031 admits a separately tagged application board/layout variant on the actual Computer for No project; a null Project never interpolates a Project key. Both use the same board engine, defaults, limits and projection/command owners.

Widgets consume stable projections and canonical records. They do not define page semantics.

- widget config changes presentation, local filtering, and layout only

## 7.1 Packet-fidelity semantic matching
Packet-fidelity checks used by VERIFIER packet preflight and SCRIBE self-check MUST ignore standalone lines whose trimmed text starts with `ContractRef:` on both the packet-text side and the file-text side before substring matching.

Required matching order:
1. Strip standalone `ContractRef:` lines from both texts.
2. Convert CRLF to LF.
3. Trim trailing whitespace per line.
4. Collapse runs of spaces/tabs to a single space.
5. Collapse 3+ blank lines to 2 blank lines.
6. Perform substring matching on the normalized texts.

Exact definition of the six steps (2026-11-25). `normalize(text)` and `matches(packet, file)` are defined by this code; an implementation must give the same result on every input and must pass every vector below.

```python
import re

def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    # step 1: drop each line whose text, after stripping leading/trailing whitespace, starts with "ContractRef:"
    # step 2: CR LF, lone CR and LF all end a line; lines are re-joined with LF
    lines = [ln for ln in re.split(r"\r\n|\n|\r", text) if not ln.strip().startswith("ContractRef:")]
    out = []
    for ln in lines:
        ln = ln.rstrip(" \t")             # step 3: trim trailing spaces and tabs
        ln = re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", ln)    # step 4: any run of spaces/tabs, leading runs included, becomes one space
        out.append(ln)
    return re.sub(r"\n{4,}", "\n\n\n", "\n".join(out))  # step 5: 3 or more blank lines become exactly 2

def matches(packet: str, file: str) -> bool:
    p = normalize(packet)
    if p.strip() == "":
        return False                      # a packet that normalizes to nothing never matches
    return p in normalize(file)           # step 6: plain substring test, case-sensitive
```

### Catalog source and drill linkage

The Progress widget ID (`widget-orchestrator-progress`) is defined in the current promoted widget catalog in `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` Appendix C (§ C.2, § C.4). Widget_System consumes that named catalog source directly and does not invent an independent catalog or additional widget cards.

The full 13-widget Progress catalog and default drill targets are:
1. `progress.run-overview` → Execution unit tree scoped to `focused_run_id`
2. `progress.current-task` → Node inspector for the active execution unit
3. `progress.lane-health` → Lane row filtered to the selected lane or worktree
4. `progress.node-throughput` → Dense node list filtered to slow or blocked nodes
5. `progress.blocked-concerns` → Concern lane filtered to `blocked` or `attention_required`
6. `progress.approval-queue` → Concern inspector showing pending approvals
7. `progress.recovery-status` → Recovery timeline for the selected concern or blocked episode
8. `progress.artifact-receipts` → Artifact browser filtered to receipt-linked runtime artifacts
9. `progress.worktree-state` → Source Control worktree row with lane, package, and run refs
10. `progress.account-pressure` → Historical `account_pressure_episode` list
11. `progress.account-switches` → Historical `account_switch_event` list
12. `progress.escalation-stack` → Project attention view focused on the shared escalation ladder
13. `progress.attention-summary` → `project_attention_item.primary_route_payload` list

Drill-through and linkage semantics (`progress` → node, `progress` → lane, `progress` → evidence) are owned by the Orchestrator UI and by the FinalGUISpec consumer contract, not by Widget_System hostability rules.

Transferred Progress labels and taxonomy:
- State labels: `queued`, `running`, `attention_required`, `blocked`, `recovering`, `degraded`, `complete`
- Action labels: `Inspect`, `Focus run`, `Open evidence`, `Request approval`, `Acknowledge`, `Dismiss`, `Resolve`, `Retry recovery`
- Alert taxonomy: `advisory`, `attention_required`, `blocked`, `escalated`, `degraded_projection`
- Event taxonomy: `run_started`, `node_started`, `node_completed`, `concern_opened`, `approval_requested`, `approval_decided`, `recovery_started`, `recovery_completed`, `artifact_published`, `account_switched`
- Condition-aging policy: advisory warnings may quiet after one stable refresh window; `attention_required` resurfaces on meaningful change or persistence; `blocked` and `escalated` never auto-quiet

Example widget-shell payload for one catalog entry (added 2026-11-25). It carries the WS-006 shell fields: widget identity and type, scope, filter, sort and display config, and projection ref.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "widget_id": "progress.blocked-concerns",
  "widget_kind": "progress",
  "host_surface": "orchestrator:progress",
  "layout_namespace": "orchestrator:progress",
  "scope": { "project_id": "proj-7f3a", "focused_run_id": "run-2041", "mode": "live" },
  "config": {
    "filter": { "states": ["blocked", "attention_required"] },
    "sort": { "key": "condition_age", "direction": "desc" },
    "display": { "max_rows": 8, "show_aging": true }
  },
  "data_ref": "projection.progress.blocked-concerns",
  "drill_target": { "action_label": "Inspect", "target": "concern_lane", "filter": { "states": ["blocked", "attention_required"] } },
  "refresh_interval_seconds": 30,
  "empty_state": "no_blocking_concerns"
}
```

Field rules:
- `widget_id` is one of the 13 catalog ids above, and `widget_kind` is `progress` for every one of them.
- `host_surface` and `layout_namespace` are `orchestrator:progress`. A Progress widget never names `dashboard` or `usage` (`### Progress-only widget hostability`, WS-030).
- `scope` is inherited from router/page scope: `project_id`, `focused_run_id`, and `mode` (`live` or `historical`). A widget never sets its own run scope; switching mode retargets every widget (WS-004, WS-007).
- `config.filter` may only narrow the page scope with the state labels above. `config.sort` and `config.display` change presentation only (WS-004).
- `data_ref` names the compact projection the widget reads. It is never a raw event stream or a bespoke query (WS-006).
- `drill_target` is the catalog's default drill target for that id, labelled with one of the action labels above. What the target page does is owned by the Orchestrator UI (WS-011).
- `empty_state` is the copy key shown when the projection returns no rows. Trust and freshness chrome comes from the shared projection-trust model, never from the widget (WS-007).

### Progress-only widget hostability

Only the Orchestrator `Progress` surface is widget-composed. `Plan Compile`, `Seams`, `Node Graph`, `Evidence`, `History`, and `Ledger` remain native views, and no other Orchestrator tab may opt into widget composition.

Tier-first widget catalog assumptions are compatibility-only; Widget_System hostability follows the Orchestrator Progress-only rule and must not broaden widgetization across native Orchestrator tabs.

The Orchestrator UI composes exactly one consumer widget: the `Progress` widget with ID `widget-orchestrator-progress`. This widget occupies a dedicated layout space within the Orchestrator UI and receives orchestrator-native runtime events, progress markers, and node-level state.

`orchestrator:progress` persists in its own layout namespace and does not share layout keys with Dashboard or Usage. Layout resets, imports, and overrides for Dashboard or Usage do not rewrite Orchestrator Progress placement.

WS-006 remains addressable as a fine-grained Widget System PlanUnit with source-span coverage.
ContractRefs, anchors or aliases, exact tokens, negative constraints, compatibility notes, stale/retired dispositions, owner boundaries, and source lineage from the source spans remain preserved.
No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, production build tasks, implementation files, or source code are created by this PlanUnit.
Widgets consume stable orchestrator projections, canonical record `/query` contracts, widget identity `/type`, scope, filter `/sort/display` config, and projection refs; they do not subscribe to raw event streams or bespoke queries.
